disposition_mapping.rationale: The council converged, against the maximalist position, that trial balance close confirmation must remain a discrete, named, human-performed attestation even where the underlying status aggregation is fully automated (hitl_designer, finance_domain, emerging_economy, pragmatist, accounting_standards; agentic_architect conceded this in round 2). The function is retained but restructured: automation does the aggregation and pre-validation, but a human must issue the confirmation every period, not only on exception, to preserve the affirmative accountability act KB-03's cutoff discipline and FSP-R-10 depend on. A manual-input fallback is specified per emerging_economy's non-negotiable against assuming machine-readable feeds exist everywhere.

Universal agreement that mechanical, schedule-matched postings can be automated but estimation-bearing entries (provisions, impairments, NRV write-downs) must keep a named, accountable human basis (KB-04, KB-10, KB-12; FSP-R-02, FSP-R-06). The step is restructured around a mandatory escalate-rather-than-resolve pattern (hitl_designer, agentic_architect) rather than split into two steps, keeping both the approved schedule and revenue cut-off evidence as explicit consumed inputs.

A strong, near-unanimous convergence (pragmatist, finance_domain, emerging_economy, agentic_architect, accounting_standards, hitl_designer conceding) holds that consolidation and FX translation already execute as one operational pass in practice and should be merged into a single step, provided the elimination-completeness requirement (KB-14) survives as a separately queryable exception queue and output rather than being absorbed into an opaque net figure. A spreadsheet-based fallback is specified per emerging_economy's deployability non-negotiable.

Merged into the same consolidation/translation step as FSP-03 for the same reasons; the translated subsidiary trial balance and translation-differences-to-OCI figure remain distinct, separately logged outputs so KB-07/KB-08's requirement that exchange differences be tracked and reported, not netted invisibly, is preserved inside the merged step rather than lost to it.

A majority of the council (pragmatist, finance_domain, emerging_economy, hitl_designer, agentic_architect) held that mapping must remain a visibly distinct step from both consolidation and drafting because chart-of-accounts misclassification is a structurally different failure mode that would not surface through drafting-quality or consolidation-exception signals. Accounting_standards and maximalist's openness to absorption into drafting is accepted only insofar as the mapped data must remain a retrievable, separately-logged artefact (which this design satisfies), but the step itself is kept distinct per the majority view, now restructured around automated mapping with a named exception queue rather than manual mapping.

Universal agreement that drafting must remain human-authored and must continue to consume the accounting policy change and prior-period error record (FSP-R-07, FSP-R-11; KB-05, KB-06). Drafting-assist tools may produce a first pass, but disclosure judgment is retained by the Financial reporting preparer.

Six of seven council members (pragmatist, finance_domain, emerging_economy, hitl_designer, agentic_architect, accounting_standards) held that tie-out must survive as an independent, human-owned checkpoint distinct from drafting and consolidation, on the ground that a generation function checking its own output is a weak control and that KB-02's evidential-trail requirement depends on independent challenge, not a log the producing engine generates about itself. Maximalist's proposal to dissolve tie-out into continuous embedded validation was explicitly conceded in round 2. The step is restructured to use automated variance pre-computation feeding mandatory human disposition, not eliminated or absorbed.

Management review and approval is retained as a non-automatable human act (FSP-R-09), with actor separation from drafting preserved (FSP-R-08). The step is restructured, not merely retained unchanged, because hitl_designer's point - conceded by finance_domain and agentic_architect - that a redesign could technically satisfy survival while gutting substance if the CFO only sees a clean draft is accepted: the input set now explicitly includes the exception and override log from upstream automated steps, so approval is informed review rather than ceremonial sign-off.

Although FSP-09 is unconstrained by design, the council largely did not treat that as license to merge it with approval: pragmatist, emerging_economy, agentic_architect, and finance_domain (who reversed his round-1 merge position in round 2) converged on keeping release structurally distinct from approval because a decision event and a near-irreversible operational/evidentiary event have different failure and recovery profiles - a failed submission must be retriable without reopening the approval decision. Only maximalist held for a merged step. The step is restructured to be agent-executable but strictly gated on a positive, logged approval token from T7, never on time elapsed or inferred completion.

steps.description: An automated aggregation layer polls subledger close-status and reconciliation-status feeds, pre-validates against a deterministic pass/fail rule set, and fails closed (no auto-confirmation) on missing or stale data; where a status feed is itself manually tracked, a manual-input fallback is supported rather than assumed away. Regardless of how clean the automated pre-check is, the GL accountant must issue an explicit, timestamped confirmation action every period - including clean passes, not only exceptions - because the control's value is the named accountability moment, not the data aggregation. Exceptions open a ticket requiring resolution or a reasoned override before confirmation can complete.
steps.name: Close readiness confirmation

steps.description: Mechanical, schedule-matched entries (standard accruals, deferral releases) post automatically with full traceability to the approved adjustment schedule line they correspond to. Any entry lacking matching support, any amount variance against the schedule, or any estimate-bearing line (provisions, impairments, NRV write-downs) is blocked from automatic posting and routed to the GL accountant, who must supply and sign a documented basis before it posts. Revenue cut-off evidence is actively verified against the schedule, not passed through silently.
steps.name: Period-end adjustment posting

steps.description: Consolidation and FX translation are run as a single operational pass by the Group accountant, reflecting how these functions already execute together in practice, with a spreadsheet-based fallback specified so the step remains executable without a specific proprietary consolidation platform. The subsidiary trial balance is translated at closing and average rates, translation differences are routed to OCI, and entity trial balances are consolidated with automated intercompany matching and elimination. Unmatched intercompany balances, elimination breaks, and rate-source anomalies are never auto-resolved or netted away; they route to the Group accountant's exception queue. The consolidated trial balance, the translated subsidiary trial balance, and the translation-differences figure remain three separately logged, independently queryable outputs even though one step produces them, so elimination completeness and exchange-difference visibility each remain separately demonstrable.
steps.name: Consolidate, eliminate intercompany, and translate foreign operations

steps.description: Standard account-to-line-item mapping applies automatically from a maintained crosswalk against the statement line-item structure. This remains a visibly distinct step from drafting and from consolidation because line-item misclassification (chart-of-accounts heterogeneity, new or unmapped accounts) is a structurally different failure mode than an elimination break or a drafting error, and would not surface through either of those steps' own quality signals. Unmapped or newly appearing accounts are never defaulted to a bucket; they are routed to Financial reporting for resolution, producing a named, auditable mapping-exception log distinct from the shared consolidation exception queue.
steps.name: Map and validate statement line items

steps.description: Statement and note drafting remains human-authored and human-accountable, even where drafting-assist or generative tools produce a first-pass text. Any content touching accounting policy changes, prior-period error correction, or revenue/FX judgment must be reviewed, edited and finalized by the Financial reporting preparer rather than passed through as an unreviewed generated draft, because these are disclosure judgments the standards require a named preparer to own.
inputs: Accounting policy change and prior-period error record
steps.name: Draft primary statements and key notes

steps.description: Tie-out survives as a discrete, human-owned checkpoint performed by a function independent of whoever produced the draft, rather than being dissolved into continuous machine validation embedded in the drafting or consolidation steps. Automated variance detection pre-computes differences between the draft and the underlying trial balance and supporting schedules, but a human must assess whether each flagged variance is explainable and material, and holds authority to kick the draft back to T5 before it reaches the CFO. This independence-of-verification-from-generation property is treated as non-negotiable: a generation function checking its own output is not an adequate substitute.
steps.name: Analytical review and tie-out

steps.description: Management review and approval remains a substantive, non-automatable accountability act performed by the CFO, structurally distinct from the drafting actor. Its input set is deliberately strengthened beyond the baseline's draft-plus-tie-out pairing to include the exception and override trail generated upstream - clean-close confirmations, estimate overrides from adjustment posting, intercompany elimination exceptions, and mapping exceptions - so approval is informed by what was auto-matched, auto-mapped, or human-overridden rather than resting on a sanitized final draft alone. Approval produces a positively logged, immutable token that is the sole trigger for release.
steps.name: Management review and approval

steps.description: Release is kept as a structurally distinct step from approval rather than merged into the same sitting, because a decision event and an operational/evidentiary event have different failure modes: release is a near-irreversible act once statements reach external parties, and a submission failure (portal timeout, filing rejection) must be retriable without reopening the approval decision itself. The release action executes only on receipt of the positive, logged approval token from T7 - never on time elapsed or draft completion - and logs its own authorizing timestamp as a distinct evidentiary artifact from the approval timestamp.
steps.name: Release / submission
